question: A sharp, single-peaked epidemic curve with cases clustered within one incubation period strongly suggests a point-source (common vehicle) outbreak rather than person-to-person spread.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Review epidemic curve interpretation in Park. A narrow, single-peak curve within one incubation period is the hallmark of simultaneous exposure from a common source (e.g., a contaminated food batch at a function).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A point-source curve rises and falls within one incubation period because all cases were exposed simultaneously. Propagated (person-to-person) curves show successive waves roughly one incubation period apart.
